bridges.statement: The diversity and recurring structure of religions are better explained by human cultural construction than by revelation from a real deity.
Claims about God and miracles warrant belief only insofar as they survive public testing with evidence proportionate to their content.
Human beings can derive meaning, moral standards, and social progress from natural capacities and shared experience without God.
Apparently indiscriminate suffering and the lack of a falsifiable pattern of divine action count against an intervening, good God.
Christian belief reasonably responds to a reality beyond human construction that illuminates the world and human existence.
Neither theism nor atheism is demonstratively provable, so both require modest, reasoned judgments under limited human knowledge.
A transcendent grounding in God explains and sustains meaning, value, human dignity, and motivation more fully than self-generated commitments.
The Christian incarnation presents God as entering history and sharing suffering, thereby supplying hope and motivation for redemptive action.
